findings.text: The drain directive names the wrong output file. argsFor() now points the freshness assertion at st.artifactName() (drain.replies.json), but compose() is still handed st.promptArtifact(dir), which hardcodes reviewFile; drainDirective() interpolates that path into "Write exactly one file, %s". A real agent following the directive writes .verdict/state/<pr>/review.json and drain then refuses no-review-artifact, so the --agent drafting path cannot complete. Spec section 5 requires the directive to name drain.replies.json as the single output file. Reproduced by rendering args.prompt through the existing drainState/argsFor test helpers: it says "Write exactly one file, .verdict/state/7/review.json" while args.abs is .../drain.replies.json.

The drain-directive test never asserts the output filename. It checks drain.json, threads.json, findings.json, the digest, defer, post nothing and untrusted data, but not drain.replies.json, so the wrong artifact path in promptArtifact() passes. Adding the required filename to this want list fails against the current code.

After --agent drafts, the JSON envelope's next tells the operator to run "drain ... --post", but this build has no --post: usage.go, docs/manual.md and the changeset all say so, and eval drain-refusals R4 asserts --post is an unknown flag. An operator following next gets a usage error; the same stale instruction is emitted by internal/core/run/service.go:745 in the launcher response.
findings.quote: return "post the drafts with verdict drain " + req.Repo + " " + req.Pr + " --post"

findings.text: Spec section 10 requires "no //nolint" for this change, but the new File struct carries a //nolint:govet directive; internal/core/drain/select.go:51 adds the same directive on Pending. AGENTS.md permits a directive with a specific reason, so this is a spec-versus-house-rule gap rather than an unambiguous lint violation.
